lessons.title: E2E allclose failures with near-identical printed tensors are rtol-boundary numeric flakes — check operand magnitudes before hunting a code bug
lessons.symptom: E2E correctness test (e.g. tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/_310p/test_classification_310p.py::test_qwen_pooling_classify_correctness) fails with `assert torch.allclose(hf, vllm, 1e-2)` while pytest prints operands that look almost equal: allclose([0.0018, 0.9980], [0.0018, 0.9982], 0.01) == False. Harness classifies it as neither code_bug nor env_flake.
lessons.root_cause: torch.allclose's THIRD positional argument is rtol, not atol — atol stays 1e-8. The pass bound is |a-b| <= 1e-8 + rtol*|b|, so for a near-zero element (prob ~0.0018 for the minority class of a binary classify head) the effective absolute tolerance is only ~1.8e-5 — tighter than torch's 4-decimal repr. fp16 accumulation differences between HF-eager and NPU kernels (~1e-4 on the near-zero probability, invisible in the printed values) exceed the bound while predictions are identical. The test is at a tolerance boundary: any kernel-numerics shift (CANN/op-plugin version, vllm build) can flip it.
fix_guidance: Read the pytest assertion repr and compute |a-b| vs atol + rtol*|b| per element — remember the 3rd positional is rtol; do not assume atol=1e-2

If the failing element is the smallest-magnitude one and the diff is within print-rounding distance (both operands print identically), treat it as a numeric flake at the tolerance boundary — do NOT perturb kernel numerics in vllm_ascend to 'fix' it
Verify non-attribution: grep the accumulated diff for the executed model path (e.g. 310P dense fp16 classify) and confirm no changed upstream file is exercised there
The e2e test file is frozen — the only legitimate source-side remedy would be evidence-based, and a numerics nudge is not; report the round as no-op/env-flake with the math in the analysis
lessons.example: step-1 e2e fix round: torch.allclose(tensor([0.0018, 0.9980]), tensor([0.0018, 0.9982]), 0.01) == False. Element 1 diff 0.0002 passes (bound 0.00998); element 0 fails because both '0.0018'-displayed values differ by ~1e-4 > bound ~1.8e-5. No diff overlap with the executed path; recorded as numeric flake.
